A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Expert-Sample work. All 24 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Appendix F's related work is relocated to Section 7 in v2 rather than deleted.

before.justification: v1 reports original expert-reduction, sampling, verification, throughput, and hyperparameter experiments in Sections 2–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds repeated-judge and alternative-judge diversity evaluations in Section 6 and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Both versions preserve the highest-ranked experts, sample remaining slots using temperature-scaled Gumbel-top-k selection, and renormalize the original gating weights. The default hyperparameters and inference procedure are unchanged; the additional judges only affect evaluation.

E1.justification: The mathematics, knowledge-reasoning, code-generation, and WikiText-2 throughput coverage is retained. The new judge study uses the existing AIME-120 Uncertain Set, without introducing a new dataset, task, or input environment.

E2.justification: Normal-temperature sampling, high-temperature sampling, and EDT remain the scaling comparators; BoN and WMV comparisons are retained. The new diversity tables compare Expert-Sample with the same two token-sampling baselines used in Section 3.3. GPT-4o and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 are judges, not competing sampling methods.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds an evaluation on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct's AIME-120 Uncertain Set using GPT-4o and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 alongside DeepSeek-R1 as diversity judges. This supplements the retained Hard Set diversity evaluation in Section 3.3; the original benchmark protocols and settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused tests of whether diversity rankings withstand repeated judging and changes of judge model. Existing hyperparameter ablations, similarity-matrix case study, expert-reduction experiments, and router-distribution analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports three judging runs, individual DeepSeek-R1 run scores, and means with standard deviations for all three judges in Tables 4–5. v1 lacks these judge-repeatability statistics, although it already reports repeated benchmark trials and standard-deviation bands in Figure 4. This does not establish additional response-generation runs.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add Uncertain Set diversity results: Expert-Sample averages 0.386 with DeepSeek-R1, 0.422 with GPT-4o, and 0.403 with Claude-Sonnet-4.6, exceeding both token-sampling baselines. These are additional evaluations, not corrections to Figure 3's Hard Set scores. Original benchmark, throughput, and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The routing and sampling equations, default configuration, and Appendix C's mathematical definition of pairwise diversity are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free expert-routing stochasticity preserves stability, improves reasoning diversity, and complements token sampling and verification. The added judge evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 now explicitly limits negligible overhead to each generated path and explains that total test-time cost grows with candidate count. Section 6 also interprets the new results as showing stable method rankings despite judge-dependent absolute diversity scores.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures retain the same sampling hyperparameters, judge prompt, LightEval and vLLM versions, model checkpoints, and A800 hardware. No implementation instructions or code/data access information are added. The new judge choices and repetition counts concern evaluation design and statistical reporting.

R1.justification: The relocated related-work section adds EAC-MoE and Ban&Pick while retaining its existing positioning. v2 also adds the GPT-4o system-card citation and two Shao et al. references attributing the unchanged throughput protocol. These are limited citation and contextual additions.

P1.justification: Most prose remains unchanged. v2 inserts a robustness section, moves related work from Appendix F into the main text, reformats the appendix overview, adds acknowledgements, and updates authorship, affiliations, and publication text. The accompanying language edits are localized.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact judge-evaluation tables as Tables 4–5; the existing appendix throughput tables become Tables 6–7. Figures 1–13 and the original table structures are retained, with localized layout changes and repagination around the additions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's diversity evaluation using one judge, v2 adds repeatability and alternative-judge evidence supporting the sampling-method ranking in Section 6. Section 5 also clarifies the distinction between per-path overhead and total sampling cost. These strengthen empirical credibility and precision, but the added validation is limited to one generator model and one AIME subset; the main method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
